newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SembCorp, SMRT to make joint statement.
newsitem.headline: SembCorp, SMRT to make joint statement.

text.p: Marine-based conglomerate SembCorp Ltd and state-owned railway Singapore MRT (SMRT) will issue a joint statement on Friday on a possible bid for a domestic telephone licence, a source to close the consortium said.
The source declined to disclose the nature of the statement.

SembCorp and SMRT announced in March they were contemplating bidding for a basic telecommunications licence, which would allow them to provide a fixed telephone service to rival the current local monopoly, Singapore Telecommunications Ltd.
The two companies said at the time they were talking to possible foreign partners who might be invited to join the bid.
There has been intense speculation over which foreign telecoms group SembCorp and SMRT would link up with.
Initial interest focused on U.S. giant AT&T but industry sources said later that company was unlikely to bid because it already had a partnership with Singapore Telecommunications.
Other rumours focused on one or all of the members of the Global One alliance of Sprint Corp, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom AG.
But for various reasons none of these companies is thought a likely entrant into the Singapore market.
Analysts said it was possible SembCorp/SMRT might announce they were not submitting a bid or had no foreign partner, or that they had a surprise name up their sleeves.
"It's getting very late in the day for anyone to come in," said John Chessher, regional telecoms analyst at Schroders.
Two other consortiums have also said they will bid for a domestic licence.

On paper, the strongest of these two bids is from a combination of British Telecom, Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp, state utility Singapore Power and state-owned Singapore Technologies Telemedia.
The other bid is from Britain's Cable & Wireless, HongKong Telecommunications Ltd, Singapore Press Holdings and Keppel Telecom.
The Singapore government has said it will award one or two licences next year for services to start from April 2000.
